jobs.title: Environmental Analyst
jobs.description:
Environmental Analyst
=====================

* Location: Richmond, California
* Program: Clean Water
* Type: Full-time
* Experience Level: Entry Level
* Salary: $82,500 to $87,500

Position Description
====================

* Posted: November 20, 2026
* First review of applications: December 7, 2026. For full consideration, please apply on or before the first review date.
* Application Close Date: The position will close on December 21, 2026 or when 125 applications have been received, whichever occurs first.

The San Francisco Estuary Institute (SFEI) is seeking an early-career scientist or engineer with an interest in environmental field studies and excellent organizational skills to join our interdisciplinary team investigating nutrient biogeochemistry and ecosystem responses in San Francisco Bay. This work will be carried out in support of the San Francisco Bay Nutrient Management Strategy (NMS; see https://www.sfei.org/programs/cw/nutrients), a research program that studies the impacts of nutrient loads on San Francisco Bay and evaluates potential management actions. Working with regional, state, federal and academic collaborators, we study the Bay’s biogeochemistry, water quality, and habitat condition using ship-based sampling, high-frequency in situ sensors, and coupled hydrodynamic-biogeochemical modeling.

This is a full-time position for a candidate who will play a key role in maintaining a network of water quality sensors and assist with data management and analysis. The candidate should have a Bachelor’s degree in a pertinent scientific field and familiarity with water quality, estuarine ecosystems, or a related area. They must be able to: (1) coordinate logistics and carry out boat-based fieldwork in an estuarine environment; (2) collect, review, and synthesize scientific data and information from various sources; (3) work well in teams as well as independently with general direction from senior scientific staff; and (4) communicate findings effectively in presentations, reports, and memoranda.

Primary position responsibilities will include:

* Contributing to the management of a distributed network of water quality sensors in San Francisco Bay.
* Coordinating, preparing for, and carrying out fieldwork on a boat.
* Occasionally lifting or carrying heavy field equipment for short durations.
* Servicing and calibrating water quality instruments in the lab.
* Assisting with maintaining telemetry equipment and troubleshooting issues with external partners.
* Conducting quality assurance and quality control (QA/QC) of NMS data and working with external laboratories to troubleshoot analyses and reporting issues.
* Assisting with project management and operations tasks for the NMS field programs (e.g., budget tracking, task management, and coordination with external collaborators).
* Assisting with writing technical reports and standard operating procedures (SOPs), and contributing to the development of posters and presentations for meetings and conferences.
* This position requires in office and/or in person presence at least 4 days per week for lab and fieldwork. Fieldwork may include 3-4 long field days (often early mornings) per month in varying weather conditions.

Qualifications
==============

Required Experience
-------------------

* Bachelor's degree in environmental science, civil or environmental engineering, oceanography, ecology, chemistry, biology, or a related field.

Required Skills
---------------

* Familiarity with environmental chemistry or environmental science.
* Strong attention to detail and organizational skills. Ability to manage competing priorities and adapt effectively in a fast-paced work environment.
* Experience with and/or the ability to lead or participate in boat or ship-based fieldwork, and to coordinate field and lab logistics.
* Ability to calibrate water quality instrumentation and conduct other lab-related tasks.
* Excellent communication, presentation and writing skills, and ability to synthesize information.
* Ability to work well in teams and work independently with general direction from senior scientific staff.
* Valid driver’s license.

Preferred Skills
----------------

* Experience calibrating and deploying aquatic instrumentation.
* Experience processing, analyzing, and visualizing data using Python or R (or similar).

Salary & Benefits Highlights:
=============================

* This will be an Environmental Analyst position. The anticipated salary range for full time employment is $82,500 - $87,500 for this position. Salary ranges take into account many factors for making compensation decisions including but not limited to experience, education, internal equity, and organizational needs. We expect to offer starting salaries at the low end of the salary range.
* Matching contributions to retirement plan (immediate vesting) (403B)
* Medical Insurance: health, vision, dental with employer and employee contributions
* 12 paid holidays
* Vacation days starting at 3 weeks accrual/year

About Clean Water
=================

SFEI's Clean Water Program provides the science behind water quality management in San Francisco Bay and the Sacramento-San Joaquin Delta. The Program is home to the Regional Monitoring Program for Water Quality in San Francisco Bay, which has tracked contaminants in the Bay for more than three decades, and to the Nutrient Management Strategy, which, since 2012, has built the monitoring, modeling, and synthesis capacity needed to understand how nutrients affect the Bay and to inform the regional Nutrient Watershed Permit. Clean Water staff work closely with the San Francisco Bay Regional Water Quality Control Board, Bay Area Clean Water Agencies, U.S. Environmental Protection Agency, U.S. Geological Survey, and academic partners.
